messages:
maya: Quick strawman for assigning prefetch/cache savings in the cost dashboard — 2-minute sketch. Idea: compute token savings per invocation (baseline_tokens - actual_tokens) and allocate credits to routes proportionally by a weighted score: tokens_saved * route_priority_weight. Show both raw and adjusted unit cost in the UI. Thoughts?
jonathan: Curious how this plays with multi-model chains where prefetch on model A benefits model B. Do we split the credit across the chain or assign to the immediate caller? :thinking:
samir: My vote is chain-aware split. We can attribute savings along the chain by walking invocation parent_id and splitting according to observed downstream token consumption. Lightweight heuristic: split by downstream model token_fraction (computed from traces) + small fixed share to the original caller. Example: 70% downstream, 30% caller.
li: UX caution: exposing too many heuristics will confuse customers. Can we present an "allocation provenance" toggle that expands into a plain text explanation + simple visualization? Default should be the most intuitive (caller gets credited) and advanced mode shows chain-split details.
maya: Agree on default = caller-get-credit. The strawman was to show both so power users can opt-in. Also want to avoid negative unit costs in the rollup when credits > charge — need guardrails.
jonathan: Guardrail idea: cap credits per-invocation to 100% of the invocation's nominal cost, and show a separate line item for "prefetch rebate" so invoice math stays sane.
samir: For implementation: we can compute a per-invocation credit metric in the router pipeline and emit as a telemetry field: `prefetch_credit_token_equiv`. Then downstream billing transform aggregates by route. Quick sketch SQL to compute route-level allocation:```sql
-- assume invocations(id, route, parent_id, baseline_tokens, actual_tokens)
with saved as (
  select id, (baseline_tokens - actual_tokens) as tokens_saved
  from invocations
  where baseline_tokens > actual_tokens
), chain as (
  select s.id, s.tokens_saved, i.route, i.parent_id
  from saved s
  join invocations i on i.id = s.id
)
select route,
       sum(tokens_saved * coalesce(route_weight,1)) / sum(tokens_saved * coalesce(route_weight,1)) as normalized_share,
       sum(tokens_saved * coalesce(route_weight,1)) as total_weighted_saved
from chain
group by route;
```
li: Nice. Two implementation flags: (1) route_weight needs to be stable (or else UI will bounce), so we should persist the weight used for a billing window. (2) sampling: we may not trace every invocation, so we need to upweight sampled traces with `1/sample_rate`.
maya: Good catch re: sampling. Also we need to handle cache-prefetch joint savings: when cache avoids tokens entirely (0 actual_tokens), attribution should prioritize the route that triggered the prefetch policy, not the route that happened to benefit later.
jonathan: That's tricky — we should store a `cache_origin_route` on the cache entry and prefer that for crediting for a TTL window. If multiple routes touch same cache key, then split by access_count during TTL.
samir: Perf note: computing chain splits at query time is expensive. Suggest precompute daily aggregates in the pipeline: emit `credits_events(route, credited_route, tokens_saved_estimate)` to a compact table. Then dashboard queries are simple sums.
li: For the console: show a hover that says "credits derived from traces & cache origin; sampling-adjusted". Also add a filter "show only credits attributed to my team" so product teams don't get spilled credits.
maya: Ops checklist: 1) add `prefetch_credit_token_equiv` to router telemetry schema, 2) add cache_origin fields, 3) store per-window route_weights, 4) aggregation job to emit credits_events, 5) UI mock and document math in docs.
deploy-bot: deploy started for aggregation-job v0.2 (pipeline-credits) by @samir — build 20240320. :rocket:
jonathan: Quick Q: how do we surface this to customers who are on Dedicated where they expect raw token billing? We should expose both "raw token usage" and "net cost after credits" with ability to export both.
li: +1. Also add an audit log page listing attribution rules applied for a billing period.
maya: I'll draft a PR with the schema changes and a small UX mock for the toggle. Assigning follow-ups: @samir to prototype aggregation job, @li to design UI copy, @jonathan to write billing guardrail docs.
jonathan: Thanks — ping me when PR is ready, I can review quickly. :+1:
li: tagging product to keep messaging consistent: @maya FYI.
maya: thanks all, will post PR link here when ready.
